newsitem.title: UK: Guinness up on better-than-forecast H1 data.
newsitem.headline: Guinness up on better-than-forecast H1 data.

text.p: Shares in British brewing and spirits group Guinness Plc gained over one percent on Thursday after the company announced better-than-expected results for the first half of this year.

Despite a warning that market conditions in Europe remained tough, Guinness shares pushed as high as 460p but slipped slightly to trade at 458-1/2p by 0731 GMT, up four pence on the day. The overall market was steady.
Guinness said pretax profits rose to 357 million stg in the first half from 340 million a year earlier. Analysts had forecast profits between 337 million stg and 353 million.
Dealers said the Guinness stock was likely to hold steady over the day but said worries about the outlook for Europe could tend to brake its performance.
"The share has underperformed in the last two months, so the downside is limited but there's little reason to rush into the stock. It's a bit of a two-way pull," one market maker said.
Dealers said they would await the results of an analysts' meeting, particularly for comments on German and French markets.
"Also, very little was said about the Far East and there's been talk of some problems there," the market maker said.
